scope: Euler Gaussian heat, cylinder Sobolev algebra, Gevrey composition, continuation, flow bootstrap, and correction-family compactness support

records.finding: Finite lists of line heat operators are assembled into a cylinder heat operator with contraction, semigroup, translation, continuity, commutation, and one-derivative estimates. Heat-operator support only.

Fixed-order complex cylinder Sobolev multiplication for q >= 6, with explicit low/high derivative envelopes, MemLp hypotheses, product bounds, and a finite algebra constant. No selected endpoint or radial observable.
Real-valued and scalar-vector versions of the fixed-order cylinder algebra and L2 product estimates. No Navier-Stokes selected-field transport.

Restriction and weighted-word identities plus base commutator forcing bounds. The forcing family is controlled by fixed Sobolev norms and an explicit 5461 factor under bounded coefficient-map hypotheses; no five-moment statement.
Factorial derivative product bounds when one factor has compact support. The theorem is a Gevrey product estimate and contains no selected witness, pressure, or radial-moment target.

Ordered-partition/Faà di Bruno estimates establish factorial-square Gevrey composition bounds under explicit pointwise jet hypotheses. This is composition regularity, not field-level moment transport.

Gevrey composition estimates with outer derivatives in L2. The hypotheses include measure preservation, measurability, MemLp derivative bounds, and pointwise jet bounds; no selected Cartesian observable equality.
Finite combinatorial partition weights and their nonnegative/successor/total-sum bounds. The file contains no PDE endpoint or physical moment construction.

Positive-radius Gevrey weighted norms control finite Sobolev state norms, with an optional coercive operator comparison. This is a continuation estimate under explicit norm hypotheses, not selected-field realization.

Concrete Gevrey and inverse-metric budgets yield a strong lower-order limit for a bounded viscous correction family, assuming correction data, Cauchy viscosity parameters, uniform norm bound, endpoint zero data, Duhamel equations, and divergence-free hypotheses. No CMI endpoint bridge.

First-hitting barrier and rational integral bootstrap close a finite flow generating-sum bound under B*R*T <= 1/8 and an explicitly assumed integral inequality. No selected witness or radial moment claim.

Finite flow derivative bounds are derived from a genuine within-time jet equation, continuity, factorial-square spatial jet bounds, and the same B*R*T <= 1/8 smallness condition. This is a bounded finite-order flow estimate only.
